title: Conversational operator scripts as idempotent microagents
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight 'microagent' runtime that turns support runbook steps into conversational, idempotent operator scripts. These microagents should be callable from the operator console, the CLI, and via an internal chat interface to accelerate common remediation flows while preserving auditability and safety.

Background: On-call engineers repeatedly run sequences of commands: gather diagnostics, toggle feature flags, promote fallback model variants, flush caches, or nudge autoscalers. Existing runbook-as-tasks work has been focused on larger templating systems but lacks a compact, interactive primitive that: (1) is safe and idempotent by default, (2) supports preflight checks and dry-run, (3) records structured audit events and context snapshots, and (4) can be invoked conversationally (short natural-language prompt + confirmations).

Proposal summary: Implement a microagent abstraction (YAML + small JS/Go shim) that declares: inputs, read-only required resources, steps (each marked idempotency-level), preflight checks, and rollback hints. The runtime executes steps with automatic checkpointing and emits structured telemetry. UX surfaces: a short operator prompt template in Console -> Quick Actions, a CLI adapter (opsctl microagent run), and a /remediate slash command for internal chat.

Design decisions: Keep execution engine minimal (no heavy workflow engine). Steps are synchronous scriptlets with explicit attestations for irreversible actions. Use a sandboxed container execution mode for commands that touch sensitive systems, and allow an opt-in 'privileged execution' switch gated by RBAC. Use existing audit log pipeline and wire a compact event schema for microagent runs (start/end/status/step-level-result/context-hash).

Non-goals: Not a replacement for long-running orchestrations or external policy enforcement systems. Not implementing machine-learning-driven decisioning in this ticket (future iteration).
acceptance_criteria: Microagent YAML schema v1 defined and documented in Confluence
PoC runtime that executes at least three example microagents (diagnostic-collect, toggle-fallback, cache-prune) in sandbox mode
Console Quick Action integration: operator can run a microagent with two-step confirmation and view structured step results
CLI adapter (opsctl) can run microagents with --dry-run and produces the same structured telemetry events
All microagent runs emit audit events to the internal audit log with step-level resolution
Unit and integration tests covering idempotency checks and preflight failures
Security review sign-off or documented exception if deferred

comments: 2025-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after oncall retro — multiple incidents slowed by manual step verification. Tagged P1 due to time-to-remediate impact.

2025-03-13 - Marco Li: Initial schema draft pushed to drive (link below). Leaning toward step-level 'idempotency' enum: safe|prepare|irreversible. Need design decision on optimistic vs pessimistic locking for resource-touched markers.
2025-03-13 - Riley Thompson: UX review scheduled 2025-03-17. Suggest exposing a compact diff preview in the confirmation modal for any step that mutates state.

2025-03-14 - Priya Nair: PoC runtime executes diagnostic-collect and cache-prune in sandbox; toggle-fallback requires RBAC gate wiring. Discovered an edge case when a step depends on ephemeral KV state — adding preflight check pattern.
2025-03-14 - Diego Ramos: Audit events schema v1 ready; mapping to our events ingestion requires a small transform. Will coordinate with observability team to ensure retention policy is appropriate.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Irreversible actions accidentally executed. Mitigation: default to dry-run and require explicit irreversible attestation with RBAC check.
Risk: Audit volume growth. Mitigation: compact event schema + sampling for high-frequency diagnostic runs.
Risk: Operator confusion between old runbooks and microagents. Mitigation: migration checklist and deprecation policy for legacy runbook endpoints.
